summary: One distinct CC BY 4.0 metal door passes Subphase 5.0 after reviewed separation of the source-welded leaf and frame. Static, actually viewed RTX front/rear captures and isolated RTX 4090 physics pass; robot/expert qualification remains pending.

component_review.0: Original horizontal bar; moving Handle with collision.
component_review.1: Original modeled U-frame after whole-face split; fixed Frame with all collision retained.
component_review.2: Original narrow window plane; moving Panel with collision.
component_review.3: Original leaf faces selected from component 1; moving solid-hull Panel with collision.

modifications: Separate the existing welded leaf and U-frame along original whole faces; preserve all source surfaces, texture coordinates and the original USDZ.

Uniform 0.75 scale and proper Y-up to Z-up rotation, placing the lower opening at the floor. Infer the hinge at the source negative-X jamb opposite the right-end bar/window detail; this maps to canonical right-handed push without mirroring geometry.
Fit Panel and Handle uniformly by 0.4% to create measured jamb/header clearance; leave the modeled fixed frame in place and collidable.

Use separate frame-part colliders around the existing concave aperture and a solid outer leaf hull. The leaf hull fills the small decorative window for contact; the original glass plane remains visible and collidable.
Start closed and already unlatched. No separate latch or lock bolt is modeled; all leaf, frame, glass and bar collisions remain enabled.
limits: The hinge location is inferred from the source jamb and bar/window layout; no mechanical hinge geometry was measured.
The 0.4% fitting and solid leaf collider are documented simulation approximations. The latter fills the decorative narrow window for collision while retaining its visual.
The 59.8-degree isolated geometry limit is not robot opening evidence; Subphase 5.1 expert qualification was not run.
